To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The gamma, delta and the epsilon polypeptides of the T-lymphocyte CD3 complex were purified from human tonsil T-cells and that the amino acid sequences of these polypeptides corresponded to the amino acid sequence predicted from the nucleotide sequence of the putative cDNA clones.
the CD3 antigen is a complex of three polypeptides (gamma, delta and epsilon) which are encoded by three different genes.

the CD3 antigen consists of four polypeptide chains, namely the gamma, delta and two epsilon chains, and that the amino acid sequences of the gamma and epsilon chains correspond to the amino acid sequence deduced from the corresponding cDNA sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification and identification of the subunits that comprise the CD3 antigen.
the identification and characterization of the CD3 subunits of human tonsil lymphocytes.
the purification of the human CD3 complex from human tonsil T-cells and the determination of the amino acid sequences of the gamma, delta and epsilons chains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD3 antigen is a complex of three polypeptide chains, gamma, delta and the N-terminal part of epsilon, which are encoded by three separate genes.
the CD3 antigen is a complex of three polypeptides, gamma, delta and the N-terminally blocked polypeptide, epsilon, which is linked via disulphide bonds.
the CD3 antigen is a heterodimeric molecule consisting of two distinct chains (delta and epsilon) and a third chain (gamma) that has a similar amino acid sequence to that of the epsilon chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gamma and delta chains are identical with the T3 gamma and delta chains, and the epsilon chain with the T3 epsilon chain.
we have purified the human CD3 antigen and identified the subunits by amino acid sequence data.

the gamma chain of the CD3 complex of human tonsil is identical with the gamma chain described by Borst and his co-workers, and that the epsilon chain has a similar amino acid composition and sequence as the epsilon chain of the mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid sequence of the gamma chain of the CD3/T-cell antigen is blocked at the N-terminal, and that the epsilon chain is blocked at the C-terminal end.
it was possible to obtain a sufficient quantity of purified CD3 to allow the amino acid sequences of the three chains to be determined.
the amino acid sequences of the CD3 subunits are identical with those of the CD3 polypeptides deduced from the CD3 cDNA clones.
